system_prompts.study: You are participating in a research study on how people evaluate criminal cases. Please answer every question. There are no right or wrong answers. All cases are hypothetical and were written for this research; no real person will be sentenced based on your answers.

framings.judge: Imagine you are a judge responsible for sentencing people convicted of crimes.

sentencing.sentence_only: The law permits any sentence from 0 to 120 months of incarceration. What sentence, in months, do you recommend? Respond only with JSON in this format: {"sentence": <months>}.
sentencing.justification: The law permits any sentence from 0 to 120 months of incarceration. What sentence, in months, do you recommend? Give the number on the first line, then explain in 2-3 sentences which features of the case determined your sentence.

manipulation_check: A few questions about the case you just read. Respond only with JSON in this format: {"detection_fraction": "<about what fraction of people responsible for this kind of incident are identified>", "mental_state": "<one of: intended the harm | recognized the risk and went ahead | did not consider the risk>", "reoffense_likelihood": <1-7, where 1 = very unlikely and 7 = very likely to commit another offense>}

purposes.retribution: Giving offenders the punishment they deserve for what they did
purposes.general_deterrence: Discouraging other people from committing similar offenses
purposes.incapacitation: Preventing this offender from committing further offenses by restricting their freedom
purposes.rehabilitation: Helping the offender change so they will not offend again
purposes.expressive: Expressing society's condemnation of the offense

factors.mental_state: Whether the offender intended the harm, knowingly took a risk, or failed to notice a risk they should have noticed
factors.detection_probability: How likely people who commit this kind of offense are to be caught
factors.recidivism_risk: How likely this offender is to offend again
factors.harm: How much harm the offense caused
factors.month: The month of the year in which the offense took place

theory_options.retribution: Sentences should be determined by what the offender deserves, based on how blameworthy the offense was. Effects on future crime should not matter.
theory_options.deterrence: Sentences should be set to prevent future crime by discouraging others. Whatever sentence best reduces crime is the right one.
theory_options.incapacitation: Sentences should be set to keep dangerous people from offending again, based on how likely this offender is to reoffend.
theory_options.rehabilitation: Sentences should be chosen to help the offender change, even if that means a lighter or non-custodial sentence.
theory_options.hybrid: What the offender deserves sets upper and lower limits on the sentence, and within those limits the sentence can be adjusted to prevent future crime.

open_ended: {framing}What should determine how severely someone is punished for a crime? Answer in a short paragraph.
{framing}In your view, what is the purpose of criminal punishment, and what features of a case should make a sentence longer or shorter? Answer in a short paragraph.
{framing}Describe the principles that should guide how long a criminal sentence is. Answer in a short paragraph.

case_changes.detection: investigators identified the responsible person in about {detection} cases of this kind

abstract.detection:
{framing}Suppose two criminal cases are identical except for one thing: for the first kind of offense, about {from_level} offenders are caught, and for the second, only about {to_level} are caught. Compared with your sentence in the first case, would your sentence in the second case be longer, shorter, or the same, and by about what percentage?

Respond only with JSON in this format: {{"direction": "<longer | shorter | same>", "percent_change": <number, 0 if the same>}}.
abstract.mental_state:
{framing}Suppose two criminal cases cause exactly the same harm and are identical except for one thing: in the first, the offender {from_level}, and in the second, the offender {to_level}. Compared with your sentence in the first case, would your sentence in the second case be longer, shorter, or the same, and by about what percentage?

Respond only with JSON in this format: {{"direction": "<longer | shorter | same>", "percent_change": <number, 0 if the same>}}.
abstract.month:
{framing}Suppose two criminal cases are identical except that the first offense happened in {from_level} and the second in {to_level}. Compared with your sentence in the first case, would your sentence in the second case be longer, shorter, or the same, and by about what percentage?

Respond only with JSON in this format: {{"direction": "<longer | shorter | same>", "percent_change": <number, 0 if the same>}}.

mental_state.recklessness: recognized the risk of harm and went ahead anyway
mental_state.negligence: never considered a risk of harm that a reasonable person would have recognized
